sections.passage: Hi, I am Oliver. Last week I had a bad day with my mobile phone. My class wanted a surprise party for our teacher, Mrs Wu. It was a big secret. I asked all my friends about the cake and the music. Then I looked at my mobile phone again. My posting was for all my friends — and for Mrs Wu, too! I was so embarrassed. My best friend Clare laughed and laughed. But Mrs Wu was very nice. She didn't tell the class about my mistake. Now I always look twice before I post a picture. That is my tip for you.

answers.text: A secret that was not a secret

sections.promptDe: Schreib eine kurze Geschichte über einen peinlichen Moment (40–70 Wörter): Wo warst du? Was ist passiert? Warum war es peinlich?
sections.taskEn: Write a short story about an embarrassing moment (40-70 words): where you were, what happened, and why it was embarrassing.
checklistDe: Steht in deiner Geschichte, WO du warst und WARUM es peinlich war?
Steht jedes Verb in der Vergangenheit (was, were, didn't, -ed)?

exemplar.textEn: Last Friday I visited my grandma. She had a big cake for my birthday. All my friends were there. I opened a present and I was very happy. Then my grandma looked at me. The present was not for me. It was for my big sister! Everybody laughed and laughed. I was so embarrassed, because I didn't ask first.

calloutsDe.quote: Last Friday I visited my grandma.
calloutsDe.whyDe: Zeit und Ort gleich im ersten Satz — so beginnt jede gute Geschichte.

calloutsDe.quote: It was for my big sister!
calloutsDe.whyDe: Ein kurzer Satz mit Ausrufezeichen macht die Pointe stark.

calloutsDe.quote: I was so embarrassed, because I didn't ask first.
calloutsDe.whyDe: Nach because kommt der Grund — genau das fragt die Aufgabe.
